source_excerpts.text:
## 3. The Fourier investigation also retained its unrestricted endpoint

For a real Boolean function \(f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}\), the target remains
\[
\boxed{
\sum_S\widehat f(S)^2
\log_2\frac1{\widehat f(S)^2}
\le
C\sum_S |S|\widehat f(S)^2
}
\]
with one constant \(C\) independent of the function and dimension. The recent paper examined in this continuation establishes further restricted cases, not this universal conclusion. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00246v2)

I worked with the **actual entropy increment under coordinate restriction**, rather than replacing it by absolute Fourier products. That distinction matters because Astra already contains a recursive counterexample to the stronger absolute-product coordinate criterion; it is not a counterexample to Fourier entropy–influence itself. 

Writing
\[
A_T=\widehat f(T),\qquad B_T=\widehat f(T\cup\{i\}),
\]
and \(e(x)=-x\log_2x\), the exact increment is
\[
\Delta_i(f)=
\sum_T\left[
e(A_T^2)+e(B_T^2)
-\frac12e((A_T+B_T)^2)
-\frac12e((A_T-B_T)^2)
\right].
\]

A dimension-free choice of an essential coordinate satisfying
\[
\Delta_i(f)\le C I_i(f)
\]
would close the usual induction. **I did not prove that choice exists.** Exhaustive checks through four variables and larger random tests do not establish it.

A broader phase-based relaxation fails outright. For
\[
F(x)=
\prod_{j=1}^{n}
\left(\sqrt{1-\epsilon}+i\sqrt{\epsilon}\,x_j\right),
\]
one has \(|F(x)|=1\), but
\[
H(F)=n h_2(\epsilon),\qquad I(F)=n\epsilon,
\]
so \(H(F)/I(F)\to\infty\) as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\). This is **not Boolean** and hence is not an FEI counterexample. It shows why normalization and unit modulus alone cannot support the proposed proof: the real Boolean constraint must do indispensable work.

## Outcome

The exact computations eliminate the strongest numerical Werner candidates and demonstrate that the attempted purity-based closure lacks sufficient information. They do not establish the all-copy theorem. The Fourier argument likewise still lacks its dimension-free inequality.

**No 8–10/10 discovery is justified by this continuation.** The accompanying files preserve the exact fractions, stored candidates, proofs of the diagnostic identities, search scopes, executable checks and unresolved steps without upgrading them into a claimed breakthrough.

source_excerpts.text:
The 8–10/10 foundational endpoint was not achieved in this session. The strongest complete result established is an asymptotically sharp theorem about Boolean Fourier entropy under restriction. It rules out a particular local proof strategy, but it does not resolve the Fourier Entropy–Influence conjecture, and its historical originality remains unestablished.
I investigated entropy couplings for union-closed families, covariance-based approaches to dimension-free concentration, and Gaussian-polynomial independence before and alongside the Fourier investigation. None yielded a complete foundational conclusion. The substantive result that survived is presented below, with its proof and exact limitations.
1. The foundational target
For a Boolean function \(f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}\), write
\[
\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E\!\left[f(X)\prod_{j\in S}X_j\right].
\]
Its squared Fourier coefficients form a probability distribution. Define its Fourier entropy and influences by
\[
H(f)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\widehat f(S)^2
       \log_2\frac1{\widehat f(S)^2},
\qquad
I_i(f)=\sum_{S\ni i}\widehat f(S)^2,
\qquad
I(f)=\sum_i I_i(f).
\]
Here \(I_i(f)\) is also the probability that flipping coordinate \(i\) changes the output.
The Fourier Entropy–Influence conjecture asks for a universal constant \(C\) such that
\[
H(f)\le C I(f)
\]
in every dimension. A restriction-based approach studies
\[
\Delta_i(f)
=
H(f)-\frac{H(f_i^+)+H(f_i^-)}2,
\]
where \(f_i^\pm\) fixes coordinate \(i\) to \(\pm1\). If every nonconstant Boolean function had a suitable coordinate satisfying \(\Delta_i(f)\le C I_i(f)\), induction would prove FEI. This approach is explicitly studied in the primary literature; it is not itself a new invention. arXiv
The calculation below establishes how badly the inequality can fail when the coordinate is prescribed rather than chosen.
2. The theorem actually established
Let
\[
h(t)=-t\log_2t-(1-t)\log_2(1-t)
\]
be binary entropy, and define
\[
D(t)
=
h(t)+1-h\!\left(\frac12+\sqrt{t(1-t)}\right).
\]
Local entropy modulus
For every Boolean function and every coordinate,
\[
\boxed{
0\le \Delta_i(f)\le D\!\left(I_i(f)\right).
}
\tag{1}
\]
Equality in the upper bound is possible only when
\[
I_i(f)\in\left\{0,\frac12,1\right\}.
\tag{2}
\]
The condition \(I_i(f)=1/2\) alone is not sufficient; the proof below gives the full equality criterion.
Nevertheless, the bound is asymptotical
